def is_plain_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a single non-empty path component: no separators, no "..", no NUL."""
    ex is_plain_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_plain_name("../secret") == False
    ex is_plain_name("sub/a.txt") == False
    ex is_plain_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_plain_name("") == False
    if name == "" or name == ".":
        return False
    if ".." in name:
        return False
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name or "\0" in name:
        return False
    return True

def read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the file `name` inside the directory `notes`, or "" if it is missing or unreadable.
    Reads happen only under `fs.sub("notes")`, and a name that is not a plain component never reaches a file outside `notes`."""
    post is_plain_name(name) or out == ""
    if not is_plain_name(name):
        return ""
    text = ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        text = fs.read_text(name) else ""
    return text
